cells: THE 2026-27 ROOKIE CLASS
Rookie candidates and inherited editorial profiles. Eligibility requires all three tests; unresolved cases remain noted. Available projections pull live from the board using Scoring Settings.
THE TEST: all three must be true
1. No more than25 NHL games in any single preceding season (exactly25 passes this test). Source: https://records.nhl.com/awards/trophies/calder-memorial-trophy
2.  NOT 6 or more NHL games in each of any two preceding seasons
3.  Under 26 years old on 15 September
A rookie is NOT the same as a draft pick. A 2021 draftee debuting at 23 is a rookie. A 2025 pick who played 77 games last season is not.
TIER 1: FUTURE STUDS  -  franchise ceiling, three names
TIER 2: GUARANTEED NHLERS  -  the roster spot is settled
TIER 3: DEPTH GUYS  -  they play, but not top six minutes
TIER 4: BUBBLE BOYS  -  the tier that costs people picks
TIER 5: MINOR LEAGUERS  -  opening in the AHL, junior or Europe

Anton Silayev (NJD), Kashawn Aitcheson (NYI), Jackson Smith (CBJ), Adam Jiricek (STL), Tanner Molendyk (NSH), Cameron Reid (NSH), Stian Solberg (ANA), Harrison Brunicke (PIT), Xavier Villeneuve (CHI), Charlie Elick (CBJ), Dominik Badinka (CAR), Ben Danford (TOR)
Goalies
Michael Hrabal (UTA), Trey Augustine (DET), Ilya Nabokov (COL), Arsenii Sergeev (CGY), Artur Akhtyamov (TOR), Carter George (LAK), Mikhail Yegorov (NJD), Pyotr Andreyanov (CBJ)
NOT ROOKIES. People will get these wrong.

Out on test 1, more than25 games in a single season:  Schaefer 82 (won the Calder), Sennecke 82, Lane Hutson 82, Demidov 82, Finnie 82, Savoie 82, Blake 81, Stankoven 81, KINDEL 77, Dickinson 72, Dvorsky 71, Snuggerud 70, Will Smith 69, Levshunov 68, NAZAR 66, Catton 66, Misa 45, Parekh 37, Howard 29 Lambert played exactly25 and is not excluded by test1; other eligibility tests require verification.
Out on test 2, 6+ games in each of two seasons:  Rutger McGroarty (24 then 8), Tristan Luneau (7, 6, 1)
Out on test 3, age:  Michael DiPietro, turns 27 before 15 September, despite only 4 career games
HOW BIG IS A ROOKIE CLASS  (2025-26 actuals)
NHL debuts
Calder eligible with at least one game
Played 20 or more
More than25 games in one prior season fails test1; exactly25 does not. Inherited counts are unverified.
Played 40 or more
Played 70 or more
Median rookie games played
Inherited class-size and graduation estimates are unverified. The first eligibility threshold is26 games, not25; both multi-season appearance and age tests also apply.

UNRESOLVED: McKenna AHL eligibility is reported, not settled (the new one-per-team CHL exception covers 19 year olds and he is 18). Roughly ten players with 6 to 24 NHL games last season have an open test 2, including Alex Bump, Owen Beck, Adam Engstrom and Joakim Kemell. None is tiered above.

readMe: Citrus Draft Kit 2026-27
Reconciled 12 September 2026 from supplied workbook, dated NHL sources and read-only production snapshots. Existing qualitative rate/GP assumptions retained; exceptions in Open Items.
Curated board: 618 skaters, 89 goalies. Roster Census covers all 1312 current directory players. Top600 uses combined Scoring Settings FPTS.
THE SEASON IS 84 GAMES, NOT 82
The new CBA expands 2026-27 to 84 games. The projection model was built on 82-game production, so two things were corrected here.
Original MODEL rows retain their 84/82-rebased GP, with83 maximum. MANUAL rows are already rebased. New live-source rows use rates at baseline1 and already-scaled GP. Do not rebase again.
2. Every goalie crease on the Depth Charts tab now sums to 84, not 82. That is 64 extra starts league-wide.
Rates are per game, so nothing else needed re-running. FPTS is always a per-game rate multiplied by games played.
PROVENANCE AND UNITS
Black rows are model output. Purple rows are MANUAL, derived by hand on 10 Sep 2026 because the model could not see them.
MODEL identifies forecast method, not guaranteed completeness. DEFAULT rows are documented cohort priors. Original MANUAL rows and injury/role decisions are retained.
Draft Board G/A/etc are inputs at Base GP, not necessarily final season totals. Player Audit, Team Totals and team tabs apply rate times GP Used. New rows use explicit baseline1.
HOW TO USE THIS
1. Open Scoring Settings and set your league weights in the blue cells.
2. Every FPTS figure, overall rank and positional rank recalculates from those weights.
3. GP Used is editable on every row. Change it and that player FPTS and rank follow immediately.
4. On draft day put an X in the Drafted column. Drafted rows grey out and strike through.
5. Filter by position, team, tier or source using the header arrows.
ONE HONEST CAVEAT
These are projections, not predictions, and nothing here is a claim of accuracy against any other system.
The manual rows are the least certain part of the workbook. Anything marked Low confidence is a judgement call, not a measurement.
ROSTER RISK, AND WHY IT HAS ITS OWN COLUMN
A rookie who gets sent down is worth zero, and that risk is not the same as a projection being wrong.
Original FPTS retains the supplied conditional roster scenario. New cohort-prior GP already includes camp uncertainty; do not multiply it by roster probability again.
Roster probability and Adj FPTS are blank when no independent probability exists. Consult Player Audit for source and volume meaning.
Roster % is editable. Anything under 70 percent turns red. Every figure is sourced in that row Flag column.
Re-check these after camp cuts. They are the fastest-moving numbers in the workbook.
WHERE THE MARKET NUMBERS CAME FROM, AND WHY THREE COLUMNS ARE MARKED INTERNAL
Citrus # is the overall rank across skaters AND goalies together, since both are scored on the same weights. It is ours and it ships.
The three amber columns are NOT ours. They were read off a third-party aggregator whose terms forbid commercial reproduction.
They stay in this workbook because private analysis is not redistribution, and they earned their place: they caught an error of 250 places.
They must never be exported into the paid kit, the app, a PDF, a social post or anything a customer sees. Amber means internal only.
The Consensus column has been removed entirely. It averaged three named writers published ranking lists.
A ranked list is an opinion someone wrote, not a fact anyone observed, so it is the one thing in this category that is genuinely owned.
Average draft position is different. It is the mean of picks that really happened, and a fact about behaviour belongs to nobody.
That is the line: we can compute market behaviour ourselves and publish it. We cannot republish what an analyst thinks. See the ADP build prompt.
audit: Reconciliation history and inherited notes
Inherited notes below describe earlier builds. Current checked results are in Player Audit, Team Totals, Roster Census, Change Log and Open Items.
STRUCTURAL FIX: THE SEASON IS 84 GAMES
The 2026-27 season is 84 games under the new CBA, confirmed by the NHL schedule release. The model was built on 82.
Every skater GP Used is now the model GP scaled by 84/82. Model GP is shown beside it so you can see the change.
Every goalie crease now sums to 84 rather than 82. That is 64 additional starts allocated league-wide.
This matters most for goalies, where two extra starts per crease go disproportionately to the starter.
WHY PLAYERS WERE MISSING, AND IT IS NOT ONE REASON
The projection set has TWO exclusion rules, not one, and only the first was obvious.
1. It is built on 2025-26 production, so anyone who did not play is invisible: Barkov, every 2026 rookie, Carter Hart.
2. It is a top-260 board, not the full league. The lowest model GP is 39, and Huberdeau played 50 games and is still absent.
So a player can be missing because he did not play OR because he did not rank. Those need different fixes upstream.
The transaction layer is genuinely current, verified across nine 2026 trades. Scraping is not the problem.
ADDED BY HAND, MARKED MANUAL IN PURPLE
18 skaters and 5 goalies were derived by hand and added. Method and confidence sit in the Flag column on every row.
Returning from lost seasons: Barkov, Seguin, Romanov, Palmieri, Foerster, Huberdeau.
Rookies: Martone, McKenna, Hutson, Frondell, Stenberg, Kantserov, Helenius, Hagens, Eklund, Protas.
Goalies holding real starts but absent from the model: Carter Hart, Soderblom, Husso, Brossoit, Levi.
Zeroed deliberately, visible but undraftable: Patrik Laine (unsigned, no PTO) and Tij Iginla (AHL-eligible, no published projection).
Method: per-game rates from the best available baseline season, adjusted for reported role, multiplied by projected games.
Point totals were sanity-checked against NHL.com 32-in-32 projections and the THN over-under lines. Divergences are noted per row.
THREE PREMISES I HAD WRONG, NOW CORRECTED
Tyson Foerster did NOT lose the season. He played 29 games, returned 2 April, and signed an 8yr/$56.8M extension in July.
Jonathan Huberdeau is the one player here who is currently NOT healthy. Confirmed 10 Sep he misses the start of the season.
Edmonton is not Andersen-first. Daily Faceoff today has Jarry starting with Levi backing up while Andersen is out into October.
WHAT IS STILL UNCERTAIN
Every rookie projection is a judgement call, not a measurement. Ferrari takes the UNDER on 7 of 10 published rookie lines,
so NHL.com projections likely carry an upward bias. Rookie rows here are trimmed below NHL.com except Kantserov and Hagens.
Most Daily Faceoff line combinations were last updated 4 July, before camp. Re-check roles around 20-25 September.
James Hagens has no promised roster spot. Tij Iginla may open in Tucson. Both could be worth zero.
RECONCILIATION, 10 SEPTEMBER 2026
All 32 creases sum to exactly 84. League total is 2,688 starts, which is 32 x 84 with nothing left over.
Every one of the 32 franchises appears on both the Draft Board and the Depth Charts. No club is missing.
Six goalies who were holding starts with no projection row have been added: Kochetkov, Murashov, Cossa, Varlamov, Hildeby, DiPietro.
That took stranded starts from 236 down to 64, and every remaining stranded start belongs to a third-stringer at 18 games or fewer.
FOUR OF MY OWN START PROJECTIONS WERE TOO HIGH AND HAVE BEEN CUT:
Kochetkov 36 to 32. The Hockey Writers say Bussi is the 1A, not a co-starter. NHL.com splits the wins 33 to 19.
Cossa 31 to 27. No published figure went above 30, and Vejmelka led the NHL with 64 appearances.
Varlamov 25 to 16. The Islanders signed Vitek Vanecek on 1 July expressly to compete for that backup job, and DFO currently lists Vanecek ahead of him.
Hildeby 25 to 22 and DiPietro 24 to 22, both to match the very heavy starter loads NHL.com projects for Vasilevskiy and Swayman.
ONE SKATER GAP I DID NOT FILL:
Michael Misa, San Jose, 2nd overall in 2025, played 45 NHL games last season and is absent from the model.
He is not a rookie-eligibility casualty, he is a top-260 cutoff casualty, which is the second exclusion rule at work.
I did not have a verified stat line for him, so I did not invent one. Add him by hand before you draft if you are in a deep league.
Also deliberately left out: Desnoyers (leg injury, may open in the AHL), Yakemchuk, Cristall, But, Simashev, Silayev, Belchetz, Gustafsson.
All are either AHL-bound or projected to bottom pairings with negligible fantasy value. Revisit them in a dynasty context, not redraft.
